outcome: Independent CRM copies that let you scope a bad change precisely and restore just the records affected, without a whole-org rollback.
overview: Customer relationship data is usually the most valuable data an organisation holds and the least protected, because the platform is a service and the common belief is that services back themselves up. They protect their platform; a bad data load, a mis-scoped bulk update or a departing administrator’s deletions are the customer’s problem. Veeam Backup for Salesforce takes independent copies of records, metadata and attachments, and — more usefully — supports comparing and restoring selectively, which is what a data-corruption event actually needs.

benefits.text: Records, metadata and attachments are copied independently into storage the customer controls
benefits.limits: The service provider protects its platform, not the customer’s data against the customer’s own errors and retention limits; that boundary is what this record addresses and it should be stated rather than implied

benefits.text: Changes can be compared over time, so a corruption event can be scoped before anything is restored
benefits.limits: Comparison depends on copy frequency; a daily copy cannot scope a change made and overwritten within the same day

benefits.text: Restore can be selective rather than whole-org, which is what a data event usually requires
benefits.limits: Backup success rate is not recoverability; only a tested restore against a stated objective evidences it, and the two are routinely substituted for one another

residency: Copies land in storage the customer chooses, including in-country object storage

notFor.situation: An organisation already running an equivalent independent CRM backup
notFor.why: A second copy of the same org duplicates cost without improving recoverability

notFor.situation: A lightly used CRM with little custom metadata
notFor.why: The recovery complexity this addresses does not exist at that scale

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Veeam implementation partner · Duration: 3–5 weeks to running copies with a first tested selective restore
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Review — object and attachment coverage map, data change pace, shared-responsibility position
2) Design — copy frequency, retention, repository location and permission scoping
3) Deploy — copies running across records, metadata and attachments
4) Test and hand over — selective restore tested, schedule handed over
deliverables: Every object type including custom objects and attachments is covered or explicitly excluded
A comparison between two copies identifies a seeded change correctly
A selective restore corrects the seeded change without a whole-org rollback
effort: 3–5 weeks to running copies with a first tested selective restore
